_comment: Maps each bundled font file to the CSS family names the generators ask for.
The generators request 'Georgia, "Palatino Linotype", "Book Antiqua", serif'
and 'sans-serif' -- none of which exist on Linux. Without these aliases every
label silently falls back to whatever the container happens to have, which
changes measureText and therefore every label position and halo box. That is a
silent, invisible drift of exactly the kind this whole rules exercise exists to
stop, so a missing family is a hard error rather than a fallback.
P052 is URW's Palatino clone -- the second entry in the generators' own stack,
so using it as the serif is a faithful reading of the intended look rather than
a substitution. It ships in Debian (fonts-urw-base35), which keeps the image
build reproducible and offline instead of pulling a font off the internet.
DejaVu Sans (fonts-dejavu-core) covers the sans-serif labels.
Once the browser stops rendering maps these files ARE the typography -- there
is no client-side font to disagree with, which removes the drift permanently.
